boundaries: Conformance is not Validation execution or a PASS label.
Schema conformance is not Identity-contract, Implementation, or Runtime conformance.
Conformance is not Admission, Acceptance, Authority, Publication, or Deployment.
claim_ceiling: This candidate defines scoped Conformance semantics only. It establishes no conformance result for any subject and no authority effect.
residue_refs: Implementation and runtime conformance remain deferred beyond CML-07.

scope.applicability: A current, scoped, evidence-backed relation asserting that one exact subject satisfies one exact contract version under one applicable conformance profile.
exclusions: A validator PASS without declared completeness for the conformance scope.
Admission, semantic truth, implementation existence, runtime behavior, publication, or deployment authority.

examples: product.json can conform to the Product Identity schema without proving a runtime Product realization.
An identity graph can satisfy endpoint and non-collapse obligations without admitting its artifacts.
domain_context.explanation: CML-07 may assess schema and identity-contract conformance for its identity artifacts. Implementation and runtime conformance remain deferred to later construction stages.

plain_language.explanation: Conformance says that one exact thing meets one exact contract for a clearly named scope, backed by enough current evidence. Passing a few checks—or matching a schema—does not automatically prove a broader kind of conformance.

boundary_conditions: Subject, contract, scope, profile, evidence, and owner are explicit.
Evidence stale against either subject or contract makes the claim not current.
Schema, identity-contract, implementation, and runtime conformance are separate scopes.
scientific_formal.formal_expression: conforms(S@digest, C@digest, Q, P@version, E) only if complete(P,Q) and current(E) and satisfies(E, obligations(C,Q)); schema_conformance(S) =/=> identity_contract_conformance(S) =/=> implementation_conformance(S) =/=> runtime_conformance(S).
scientific_formal.normative_statement: Conformance is a relation among an exact subject S, exact contract C, declared scope Q, applicable profile P, current evidence set E, and assessment owner. It may be asserted only when P declares E sufficient for every obligation in Q. Different conformance scopes remain orthogonal and cannot be inferred from one another.

notation.meaning: The exact subject whose conformance is assessed.
The exact contract and version assessed.
The current evidence set used for the assessment.

testable_conditions: Every obligation in the declared scope maps to current evidence or a causal NOT_EVALUABLE result.
No narrower conformance claim is promoted into a broader scope.
A conformance assertion carries no admission or publication effect.
